result:
I want to talk about how absurdly, stupidly beautiful the world is when you actually pay attention.

Right now, as I'm typing this, there's a house spider living in the corner of my window. She's been there for three weeks. Every morning she rebuilds her web after the wind destroys it, and every evening she sits in the exact same spot like a tiny Zen master. I’ve named her Deborah. Deborah has more patience in one of her eight legs than most humans have in their entire nervous system.

Yesterday I watched her catch a fly and I felt something I can only describe as... vicarious pride? Like “that’s my girl.” Then I realized I was emotionally invested in a spider and had to sit down for a while.

The older I get, the more I’m convinced that the meaning of life is just *noticing*. Noticing how the light changes at 6:47pm in October. Noticing that your friend’s laugh has changed slightly since last year because life has been hard on them. Noticing that the way steam rises from coffee looks exactly like galaxies forming if you squint.

We’re all just temporary arrangements of atoms that somehow learned to feel melancholy when it rains and euphoric when the first chord of our favorite song hits. That’s insane. That’s miraculous.

I keep a small notebook where I write down one ridiculous observation every day. Recent entries:

- “The way some people say ‘umm’ sounds like they’re buffering”
- “My houseplants are judging me and they have every right to”
- “Why does nostalgia hurt in the shoulders specifically?”

There’s this quiet rebellion in just... refusing to be numb. In letting yourself be moved by stupid things. The way your dog looks at you when you come home. The fact that bananas are technically berries but strawberries aren’t. That one specific memory from when you were nine that randomly surfaces and makes you cry in the grocery store for no reason.

The universe spent 13.8 billion years setting up the exact conditions for you to exist and eat cereal while watching reality TV and feeling things about fictional characters. That’s either the most beautiful cosmic joke ever told or the most loving act of creation imaginable. Probably both.

Anyway. Deborah just caught another fly. I’m weirdly emotional about it.

What random thing has been breaking your heart or blowing your mind lately?
